entities.name: Query protein (80 aa)
observations: The 80-residue sequence exactly matches reviewed Vibrio parahaemolyticus ZapB Q87T24 at 100% identity and full coverage.
Predicted molecular weight is 9411.444 Da, theoretical pI 4.517, GRAVY -0.86, and charge at pH 7 approximately -10.36.
Pfam scanning identifies the ZapB domain PF06005.19 across residues 1-78 with i-Evalue 9.7e-27.
The sequence is strongly acidic and hydrophilic, consistent with a soluble coiled-coil protein rather than a membrane protein or enzyme.

entities.name: ZapB Q87T24
observations: Reviewed Vibrio parahaemolyticus cell division protein; the query sequence is an exact sequence match.
ZapB is a non-essential, abundant cell division factor required for proper FtsZ Z-ring formation.
ZapB localizes to the cytoplasm and septum at mid-cell in an FtsZ-like pattern.
ZapB forms homodimers through coiled-coil ends and can polymerize; it interacts with FtsZ.

entities.name: ZapB domain PF06005
observations: Pfam domain PF06005.19 spans residues 1-78 of the query sequence with i-Evalue 9.7e-27.

entities.name: FtsZ-dependent cytokinesis
observations: ZapB is annotated in FtsZ-dependent cytokinesis and cell septum assembly.
